chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated on the authority of some of our companions, elevating it, saying:

A man came to al-Hasan ibn `Ali (peace be upon them both) and said to him: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, describe your Lord to me so that I can see Him as if I were looking at Him." Al-Hasan ibn `Ali (peace be upon them both) bowed his head in silence for a long time, then raised his head and said: "All praise is to Allah, who has no known beginning and no reaching end, no perceivable before and no limited after, no limit of 'until' and no distinct form that can be divided, nor variation in description that reaches a limit. Thus, intellects and their imaginations cannot grasp His description, nor thought and its fleeting notions, nor minds and their perceptions can describe Him such that they say: 'When?' And no beginning from 'what,' no appearance upon 'what,' no concealment within 'what,' nor one who leaves [creation] so why not? He created the creation, so He was Original and Unprecedented. He originated what He unprecedented and unprecedented what He originated. He did what He intended, and intended what He extended. That is Allah, the Lord of the Worlds."
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Hasan describe the attributes of Allah to convey His transcendence and lack of physical form?
ai.summary: This hadith, a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse on *Tawhid*, illustrates the method of *Tanzih* (negation of attributes) to affirm divine transcendence beyond human sensory perception. Imam al-Hasan (AS) systematically negates spatial, temporal, and physical limitations—such as direction, body, and composition—to demonstrate that Allah’s essence is incomprehensible to the intellect, thereby refuting anthropomorphism (*Tashbih*). This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between Allah’s essence and His actions, establishing that while He is the Creator, He cannot be contained by created categories.
